method_card.title: Rates of Change & Iteration (reference)
method_card.content:
The rate of change at a point is the gradient of the tangent there: pick two points on the tangent and compute rise ÷ run.

An iterative process uses \(x_{n+1} = f(x_n)\). Start at \(x_0\), substitute to get \(x_1\), then feed that back in for \(x_2\), and so on until the values settle. Keep the full calculator value between steps and round only at the end.

A sign change in \(f(x)\) locates a root; the trapezium rule estimates the area under a curve.

steps.say: A phone game gives you tokens. You start with 100. Each round the app halves your tokens, then hands you 30 bonus tokens. No algebra, just do the two sums.

steps.hint: Halve 100 to get 50, then add the 30 bonus.

steps.say: Now take that new total, 80, through the same rule again.

Each new total was the old total put through one rule: halve, then add 30. Feeding an answer back into the same rule, over and over, is called iteration. In algebra we write the rule as \(x_{n+1} = \frac{x_n}{2} + 30\), with \(x_0 = 100\) the starting pile. The other half of this lesson reads a rate of change straight off a graph: the steepness (gradient) of the line, rise ÷ run.
